sentences.text: Palaeocursornis is classified as a dubious genus of avemetatarsalian, likely an azhdarchoid pterosaur.
It belongs to the suborder Pterodactyloidea, is part of the superfamily Azhdarchoidea, and is placed within the family Azhdarchidae.
The genus Palaeocursornis was established by Kessler and Jurcsák in 1986, originally based on a species first described as Limnornis corneti in 1984.
However, the bones were initially described as Limnornis corneti, but this genus name had already been used for the curve-billed reedhaunter (L. curvirostris), an ovenbird.

It was initially considered a flightless paleognath bird, possibly a ratite, and later as an ornithuromorph bird or non-avian theropod. However, a re-evaluation suggested the specimen was not a femur but the humerus of a pterodactyloid pterosaur similar to Azhdarcho.
Furthermore, the bones attributed to the new taxon appeared to belong to two different species that were possibly not even closely related.

The fossil was found in Early Cretaceous Berriasian rocks dating to around 143 million years ago from a mine at Cornet near Oradea in northwestern Romania. The animal lived on an archipelago of volcanic and coral islands located towards the east of the Piemont-Liguria Ocean.
The time range for Palaeocursornis is from 143.1 to 137.05 million years ago.
In 2025, Thomas and McDavid suggested that Palaeocursornis is a dubious genus of tapejaroid.
The type species listed in the Paleobiology Database is Palaeocursornis biharicus.
